answer:
No, you should not lime this field. Liming is used to raise soil pH in acidic soils [S1], but the soil pH on this parcel is 8.8 (SSURGO soil survey (dominant component of the map unit)), which is already alkaline and above the optimal range of 6.5 to 8.2 for alfalfa. 

At this pH level, adding lime would make the soil even more alkaline. In fact, soils with a pH of 8.8 are often calcareous, meaning lowering the pH is difficult and rarely economic. 

Confirm the soil pH with a laboratory soil test before applying any soil amendments.
